schema_roundtrip_drill.detail: apply -> rollback -> reapply convergence: post-down hash equals the pre-up baseline and the re-up hash equals post-up. Reproduced locally against a scratch postgres:16 seeded from the baseline replay root, where pre-up (6a6f1c70e9…) differs from post-up (fd7f6a7e0a…) — so the hash is demonstrably sensitive to this migration rather than blind to it.

live_schema_parity.workflow: Live Schema Parity / Live Schema Parity
live_schema_parity.detail: PASS at this anchor, and legitimately so before production apply. scripts/ops/compare-databases.ts queries pg_class, information_schema.columns, pg_constraint, pg_indexes, pg_policies, pg_trigger and pg_extension — and no pg_proc. This migration creates a function and no relation, so it produces no parity finding. A relation-creating migration would fail here until applied to production; that ordering constraint does not arise for this lane.

acl_proof.detail: PUBLIC revoked, and anon/authenticated revoked by name where those roles exist. The archived UTV2-1177 text set no ACLs at all, so replaying it would have created a SECURITY DEFINER writer into the certification ledger that is EXECUTE-to-PUBLIC and therefore reachable by anon through PostgREST. REVOKE FROM PUBLIC alone is not sufficient on Supabase.

reversibility.detail: The down script drops exactly one function. It owns no rows; certification ledger rows are append-only and survive it.
